Messages.Author: Morgan Vening
Messages.Body:
On 9 Mar 2005 12:11:17 -0800, "2Extreme4U" <xruby...@hotmail.com>
wrote:

>Quick question on the black glove:
>
>This weapons does Strenght + 1 aggravated damage and is a glove. Does
>that mean that if I immortal grapple someone, I can use my glove to
>make strenght + 1 aggravated damage?

No. Black Glove is a "Unique melee weapon.". Hence it's a Melee Weapon
strike. Hence it is not a Hand Strike. Hence it is not permissable by
the terms of Immortal Grapple.

Morgan Vening

Messages.Author: John Flournoy
Messages.Body:
2Extreme4U wrote:
> Quick question on the black glove:
>
> This weapons does Strenght + 1 aggravated damage and is a glove.
Does
> that mean that if I immortal grapple someone, I can use my glove to
> make strenght + 1 aggravated damage?

No. Using a weapon is not a hand strike, which is what Immortal Grapple
limits you to.

The fact that the card name includes 'Gloves' does not override the
fact that it's a (melee) weapon by card text. You can no more use a
Black Glove while Immortal Grappling than you can a Sengir Dagger or
Kali's Fang.

Black Gloves' card text also does not alter your hand damage, so you'd
be striking for whatever your base strength is.

> In the case of Lazverinius using a torn signpost and striking for +3,
> effectively inflicting 9 Aggravated damage which would probably burn
> most vamps in that game unless they can prevent!

A very nasty combo, but not one you can use with Immortal Grapple.

> Thanks!

-John Flournoy
